mainTopic: Which חטאת blood requires כיבוס, and רבי אבין's and לוי's questions about the blood of a bird offering and of blood sprayed from garment to garment
overview: The תורה says that if blood of a חטאת splashes on a garment, the garment must be washed (כיבוס). The גמרא first finishes showing that the inner sin offerings share many more features with the eaten animal חטאת than the bird offering does, so the bird חטאת is the one left out. רב יוסף gives another source: "יאכלנה" shows the excluded offering is an eaten one, and "זאת" shows there is an exclusion at all. רבה reads "אשר יזה" (sprinkling) to mean the passage is mainly about the inner offerings. "תורת" then adds the outer animal חטאת, and "זאת" leaves out the bird, because the animal offering is far more similar. רבי אבין then asks two questions about bird blood: is carrying a bird into the היכל with blood in its neck like bringing in a vessel, and is bird blood gathered from the floor valid? Proofs are suggested for each, and both are rejected. Finally לוי asks whether blood that sprays from one garment onto another still needs washing. רבי answers yes either way, relying on רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Finishing the list of shared features
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its list of ways that חטאות הפנימיות are like the eaten animal חטאת: קרן, אצבע, חודה and אישים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and the corner of the altar, and the finger, and the edge of the corner, and the altar fires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it started before this section. The list explains why the inner sin offerings belong with the eaten animal חטאת for the law of כיבוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inner sin offerings and eaten animal sin offerings both have blood put on a קרן of an altar, with the priest's אצבע, on its edge (חודה), and both have parts burned on the altar fires (אישים). A bird חטאת has none of these features. That is why the inner offerings are included and the bird offering is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: A corner (horn) of the altar, where the blood is placed
Finger: the priest puts the blood on with his finger
Its edge: the sharp edge of the altar's corner
The altar fires: parts of the animal are burned on the altar

phrases.english: and the corner, and the finger,
and its edge, and the altar fires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, begun before this section, to the question of which חטאת to include and which to leave out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חטאות הפנימיות are included because they share many features with the eaten animal חטאת: קרן, אצבע, חודה and אישים, along with the features listed before.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why include the inner sin offerings and leave out the bird sin offering, and not the other way around?

steps.title: Challenge: the bird offering seems more similar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: חטאת העוף should be the one included, because its blood goes on the outer altar and it is eaten, just like the animal חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! The bird sin offering should have been included, since it is like it in the outer altar and like it in being eaten!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice it just made. It argues that the bird offering is actually closer to the eaten animal חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eaten animal חטאת has its blood placed on the outer altar (חוץ), and its meat is eaten. The bird חטאת shares both of these features. Inner sin offerings share neither of them, since their blood goes inside and they are burned, not eaten. So maybe the bird offering should be included instead.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary: introduces the opposite argument
The bird sin offering
To include (in the law)
Outside: here, the outer altar
Eating: the offering is eaten by the כהנים

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה, חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי –
phrases.english: On the contrary, he should have included the bird sin offering –
since it is like it in being on the outer altar,
phrases.notes: "It" is the eaten animal חטאת that the verse is talking about.

phrases.english: and like it in being eaten!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 1 by pointing out features the bird offering shares with the eaten חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to include חטאות הפנימיות and leave out חטאת העוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bird offering shares two key features with the eaten animal חטאת (outer altar and being eaten), so it seems to be the closer match.

steps.title: Answer: the inner offerings share more features
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the shared features of the inner sin offerings are more numerous, so they win.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its original choice. The inner offerings share more features with the eaten חטאת than the bird offering does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird offering has two points of likeness, but the inner offerings have a long list (animal, vessel, קרן, אצבע, חודה, אישים, and more). When we must choose which case to include, we pick the one with more features in common. So the inner offerings are included and the bird offering is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Those (features)
Are more numerous

steps.whatToRemember: By counting shared features, the גמרא includes חטאות הפנימיות in כיבוס and leaves out חטאת העוף.

phrases.english: Those are more numerous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing of similarities: the larger number of shared features decides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird offering, which is outer and eaten, should be the one included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inner offerings share more features, so they are included and the bird offering is left out.

steps.title: רב יוסף: "יאכלנה" points the exclusion at an eaten offering
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different source. The word "יאכלנה" ("shall eat it") means "this one and not another", so the verse leaves out a type of חטאת that is eaten, which is the bird offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The verse says "shall eat it": to this one and not to another. The verse excluded from among the eaten offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a new way to show that bird חטאת blood does not need כיבוס. He reads it straight from the verse, with no need to compare features.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse talks about a חטאת that is eaten ("יאכלנה"). The word "it" limits the law to this offering and not to another one. So whatever is left out must also be an eaten offering. Inner offerings are not eaten, so the one left out must be the bird חטאת, which is eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: "He shall eat it" (ויקרא 6:19)
To this one and not to another
Offerings that are eaten
The verse excluded (left something out)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a source from the verse itself, not just from comparing features, for why חטאת העוף is not part of כיבוס.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: The verse says:
"shall eat it": to this one and not to another;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:19

phrases.english: the verse excluded from among the eaten offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא: יֹאכְלֶנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same result as steps 1–3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exclusion from כיבוס falls on an eaten חטאת, meaning חטאת העוף, as shown by the word "יאכלנה".

steps.title: Then why do we need "זאת"?
steps.stepSummary: If "יאכלנה" already does the excluding, the word "זאת" seems to be extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why do I need "this"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף. If his word does the job, the word "זאת" seems to have no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the exclusion was learned from "זאת" ("This is the law of the חטאת"). If "יאכלנה" both excludes and tells us what is excluded, then "זאת" adds nothing. A word in the תורה is not supposed to be extra.

keyTerms.meaning: "This" (ויקרא 6:18), the word used earlier to exclude
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: But then why do I need "this"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's approach in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's use of "יאכלנה" as the source of the exclusion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "יאכלנה" does all the work, the word "זאת" would be extra.

steps.title: Both words are needed
steps.stepSummary: Without "זאת", we would think "יאכלנה" is just the normal way the verse speaks. So "זאת" shows there is an exclusion, and "יאכלנה" shows which offering is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for "this", I would have said that "shall eat it" is just the verse's normal way of speaking. So it teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each word has its own job. "זאת" tells us something is left out, and "יאכלנה" tells us what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, "יאכלנה" could just describe what normally happens to a חטאת, with no extra lesson in it. "זאת" teaches that some חטאת is left out. Once we know that, "יאכלנה" tells us the excluded one is an eaten offering: the bird חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
The normal way the verse speaks (no special lesson)
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף: "זאת" shows that a חטאת is excluded from כיבוס, and "יאכלנה" shows it is an eaten one, so חטאת העוף does not need כיבוס.
steps.confusionAlert: "קא משמע לן" here refers back to the word "זאת". "זאת" teaches that there is an exclusion at all. It does not tell us which offering is excluded.

phrases.english: If not for "this", I would have said:
"shall eat it" is just the verse's normal way of speaking;
so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: "It" is the word "זאת", which shows that something really is being left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word has its own job: one shows there is an exclusion, the other shows what it is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "יאכלנה" alone might be just a description, with no exclusion.
steps.terutzMaskana: "זאת" creates the exclusion, and "יאכלנה" points it at an eaten offering, the bird חטאת.

steps.title: רבה: The verse speaks about sprinkled blood
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the words אשר יזה show that the law of כיבוס is about sin offerings whose blood is sprinkled, which are the inner ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: the פסוק says 'that it shall be sprinkled.' So the פסוק is talking about offerings whose blood is sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a different source for why the inner sin offerings need כיבוס. He points to the words אשר יזה in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we saw that the inner sin offerings were included by comparing them to the eaten ones. רבה says this is not needed. The word הזאה (sprinkling) is the word the תורה uses for the inner sin offerings, so the פסוק is about them directly.

keyTerms.meaning: "That it shall be sprinkled" (ויקרא 6:20)
Sprinklings of blood
Washing a garment that blood splashed on

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The verse says: "that it shall be sprinkled" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20

phrases.english: the verse is speaking about sprinklings.
phrases.notes: Sprinkling is the word used for the inner sin offerings, whose blood is sprinkled inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source, alongside רב יוסף's, for which sin offerings need כיבוס
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of כיבוס is mainly about the inner sin offerings, because the פסוק uses the language of sprinkling.

steps.title: But the משנה says the verse is about eaten offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה: the משנה says the פסוק speaks only of eaten sin offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: even though the פסוק speaks only about offerings that are eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה by quoting the משנה, which says the פסוק is only about eaten sin offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק were mainly about the inner sin offerings, as רבה says, the משנה could not say it speaks only of eaten ones. The words of the משנה seem to contradict רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offerings that are eaten (the outer ones)

phrases.english: But it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
phrases.english: even though the verse speaks
only about the eaten ones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the כיבוס passage is about sprinkled (inner) offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the passage speaks only of eaten offerings, which contradicts רבה.

steps.title: The משנה means scouring pots, not washing clothes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's words apply to scouring and rinsing the pots. For washing clothes the פסוק says אשר יזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is about scouring and rinsing. But for washing clothes, it is written 'that it shall be sprinkled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה was talking about a different law in the same passage, the scouring and rinsing of pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The passage has more than one law. Scouring and rinsing pots only applies to eaten offerings, since only those are cooked. Washing clothes is tied to אשר יזה, so it is about the sprinkled (inner) offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Scouring a copper pot an offering was cooked in
Rinsing the pot with water
"Regarding": limits a statement to one topic

phrases.english: That is regarding scouring and rinsing,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21. A pot used for cooking the offering must be scoured and rinsed.

phrases.english: but regarding washing –
"that it shall be sprinkled" is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה's statement to a different law in the passage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'only eaten ones' applies to the whole passage, including כיבוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only to scouring and rinsing. כיבוס follows אשר יזה.

steps.title: Then the משנה's word order is backwards
steps.stepSummary: If the inner offerings are the main subject, the משנה should have listed them first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'both the eaten ones and the inner ones'? It should have said 'both the inner ones and the eaten ones'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of words in the משנה, based on רבה's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the main case is listed first. According to רבה the inner offerings are the main subject of כיבוס, and the eaten ones are only added. So the משנה's order does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: "If so": takes the answer and finds a problem with it
Inner sin offerings, whose blood is brought inside
"It should have said"

phrases.english: If so,
"Both the eaten ones and the inner ones"?!
It should have said "both the inner ones and the eaten ones"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֶחָד הַנֶּאֱכָלוֹת וְאֶחָד הַפְּנִימִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer and finds a problem in the משנה's wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The word order of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The main case (the inner offerings, according to רבה) should be listed first.

steps.title: Switch the order in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says to learn the משנה with the inner offerings first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn it as: 'both the inner ones and the eaten ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא simply fixes the wording of the משנה so that it fits רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving up on רבה's source, the גמרא changes the order of the words. Now the inner offerings, the main subject, come first.

phrases.english: Learn it as: "both the inner ones and the eaten ones."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the word-order challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's order shows that the eaten offerings are the main case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should be learned with the inner offerings first.

steps.title: Then the bird sin offering should need washing too
steps.stepSummary: If sprinkling is the key, חטאת העוף should also need כיבוס, since its blood is sprinkled too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the bird sin offering too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question on רבה: חטאת העוף also has sprinkled blood, so why doesn't it need כיבוס?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה linked כיבוס to the word sprinkling. The תורה also uses that word for חטאת העוף. So by רבה's logic it should be included as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird sin offering
"Also, too"

phrases.english: If so, the bird sin offering too!
phrases.notes: Its blood is also described as sprinkled, in ויקרא 5:9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge on רבה's sprinkling source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sprinkling also applies to חטאת העוף, so it should need כיבוס.

steps.title: The word זאת leaves out the bird offering
steps.stepSummary: The תורה excludes חטאת העוף with the word זאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One excluded it with the word 'this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word זאת ('this is the law of the sin offering') keeps חטאת העוף out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זאת is a limiting word: 'this one and not others.' According to רבה, it is the word that leaves out the bird offering, even though its blood is sprinkled.

keyTerms.meaning: "Excluded": a word in the פסוק narrows the law
"The Merciful One": the תורה
"This": a limiting word

phrases.english: The Merciful One excluded it with "this."
phrases.notes: From ויקרא 6:18, "This is the law of the sin offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the bird offering challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every sprinkled offering, including the bird, needs כיבוס.

steps.title: Then the outer sin offering should be left out too
steps.stepSummary: If זאת limits the law, the outer (eaten) sin offering should also not need כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the outer one also should not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if זאת limits the law to the sprinkled inner offerings, then the outer sin offering should also be left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the main subject is the inner offerings. The outer sin offering's blood is placed, not sprinkled. If זאת is limiting, why should the outer one be included?

keyTerms.meaning: An outer sin offering, whose blood goes on the outer altar

phrases.english: If so, the outer one also should not!
phrases.notes: He means it shouldn't need washing either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the זאת answer and pushes it further
steps.kashyaTarget: Using זאת as a limiting word
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If זאת narrows the law to sprinkled offerings, the outer sin offering, which is not sprinkled, should also be left out.

steps.title: The word תורת adds the outer sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The תורה includes the outer sin offering with the word תורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One included it with the word 'the law of.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word תורת ('the law of the sin offering') adds the outer sin offering back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק has a limiting word (זאת) and an adding word (תורת). זאת leaves out the bird offering, and תורת brings in the outer animal offering. So, according to רבה, the inner and the outer animal sin offerings need כיבוס, but the bird offering does not.

keyTerms.meaning: "Included": a word in the פסוק widens the law
"The law of": a word that adds

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה: אשר יזה makes the inner sin offerings the main subject of כיבוס. תורת adds the outer animal sin offering. זאת leaves out חטאת העוף.
steps.confusionAlert: Here רַבִּי does not mean a rabbi. It is a verb meaning 'included,' the opposite of מיעט.

phrases.english: The Merciful One included it with "the law of."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the outer sin offering challenge and completes רבה's approach
steps.terutzResolutionType: An adding word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: זאת leaves out everything except the inner offerings.
steps.terutzMaskana: תורת includes the outer animal sin offering, so only the bird offering is left out.

steps.title: Why include one and exclude the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we decided that זאת excludes the bird חטאת and תורת includes the outer animal חטאת, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next move: why did we pick these two particular offerings for including and excluding?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 13 and 15 we had one word that excludes (זאת) and one word that includes (תורת). Either word could be applied to either offering. So the גמרא wants a reason for matching the words to the offerings the way we did.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? (Why did you choose this way?)

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He means: why did you apply זאת to the bird and תורת to the outer animal חטאת, and not the other way around?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the include/exclude words from steps 13 and 15 were assigned
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for including the outer animal חטאת rather than the bird חטאת

steps.title: The animal sin offering is much more similar
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense to include the outer animal חטאת, because it shares seven features with the inner חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the animal sin offering should be included, since it is an animal, it is slaughtered in the north, its blood is caught in a vessel, put on the corner of the altar, with the finger, on the edge, and parts are burned on the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the outer animal חטאת is the better choice to include, because it is so similar to the inner חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא lists seven things the outer animal חטאת and the inner חטאת have in common: both are animals, both need שחיטה in the north, both need קבלה in a כלי, both have blood put on a קרן, with an אצבע, on the edge, and both have parts burned in the אישים. A bird חטאת has none of these, so it is the one to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it stands to reason
Slaughtering on the north side of the courtyard
Catching the blood in a vessel
Corner of the altar
The fires of the altar

phrases.english: It makes sense that the animal sin offering
should have been included,
since it is an animal, slaughtered in the north,
and its blood is caught in a vessel, put on the corner, with the finger,
and on the edge, and parts go on the fires.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא חַטַּאת בְּהֵמָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The outer animal חטאת shares seven features with the inner חטאת, so it is the one to include

steps.title: But the bird offering is also sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the bird חטאת should be included, since its blood is sprinkled, just like the inner חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, the bird sin offering should have been included, since it has sprinkling like it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: the bird חטאת also has a strong point in common with the inner חטאת, which is הזאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 12 the גמרא said that sprinkling seemed to be the key to the כיבוס law. The תורה uses the word sprinkling (הזאה) for both the bird חטאת and the inner חטאת, while for the outer animal חטאת it speaks of placing the blood (נתינה). So maybe the bird is the better match.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Sprinkling of the blood

phrases.english: On the contrary, the bird sin offering
should have been included,
since it has sprinkling, like it!
phrases.notes: Like it: like the inner חטאת, whose blood is also sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to include the animal חטאת over the bird חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bird חטאת shares הזאה with the inner חטאת, which seemed to be the key feature

steps.title: More shared features wins
steps.stepSummary: The animal חטאת wins because it has more things in common with the inner חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the seven shared features of the animal חטאת outweigh the one shared feature of the bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird חטאת shares only one thing (הזאה) with the inner חטאת. The animal חטאת shares seven. When we must choose which one the תורה meant to include, we go with the one that is more similar overall.

keyTerms.meaning: They are more numerous

steps.whatToRemember: זאת excludes the bird חטאת and תורת includes the outer animal חטאת, because the animal חטאת has many more features in common with the inner חטאת.

phrases.english: Those are more numerous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing similarities: more shared features decide
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling alone might make the bird the better match
steps.terutzMaskana: The many shared features of the animal חטאת win

steps.title: A bird sin offering carried inside with blood in its neck
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין asks: if a bird חטאת is brought into the היכל with its blood still in its neck, is it disqualified?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין asked: a bird sin offering whose blood was brought inside while in its neck, what is the law? Is its neck like a service vessel, so it becomes disqualified? Or is it like an animal's neck, where the תורה said 'of its blood' and not its flesh?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רבי אבין asks whether carrying a bird חטאת into the היכל, with its blood inside its neck, disqualifies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An outer חטאת is disqualified if its blood is brought inside the היכל in a vessel. A bird has no vessel; its blood is sprinkled straight from its neck, so maybe the neck acts like a כלי שרת. Or maybe the neck is just part of the body, like an animal's neck, and the פסוק only disqualifies bringing in the blood, not the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (an open question)
Its neck
A service vessel used in the בית המקדש
Inside (into the היכל)
Or perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about carrying a cup of blood inside. The blood is still in the bird's body, and the question is whether the neck itself counts like a vessel.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin asked:
A bird sin offering whose blood one brought
inside, in its neck, what is the law?
Is its neck like a service vessel, so it is disqualified?
phrases.notes: With a bird, the blood is sprinkled right from the neck, so the neck does the job a vessel would do.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is like the neck of an animal,
where the Merciful One said 'of its blood,' and not its flesh?
phrases.notes: ויקרא ו:כג

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, building on the point that a bird's blood is not caught in a vessel
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a bird's neck counts as a vessel for the rule of blood brought inside

steps.title: Proof from a bird that jerked inside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a bird that jerked its way inside and came back is valid, which suggests that if someone brought it in, it is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if it convulsed, went inside, and came back, it is valid. This implies that if he brought it in, it is disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבי אבין's question from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a bird that went inside on its own by jerking is still valid. The גמרא reads this closely: it only says 'on its own,' which implies that if a person carried it inside, it would be disqualified. That would mean the neck counts like a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: It convulsed / jerked
This implies (an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If it convulsed, went inside, and came back, it is valid.
phrases.notes: After the bird is killed, it can still jerk around, and here it jerked its way into the היכל.

phrases.english: This implies that if he brought it in, it is disqualified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question of step 20
steps.raayaObject: That a bird's neck is like a כלי שרת, so bringing it inside disqualifies
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a bird that convulsed into the היכל, read by inference

steps.title: The same inference would fail for animals moved to the south
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Using that logic, a ברייתא about קדשי קדשים would wrongly suggest that carrying an animal to the south side disqualifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your reasoning, look at the ברייתא about קדשי קדשים: if the animal jerked, went to the south side and came back, it is valid. Would you then say that if someone carried it to the south, it is disqualified?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 21. It shows that the same kind of 'it went by itself, so if someone carried it, it's bad' reasoning leads to a wrong answer somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי קדשים must be slaughtered in the north, but moving them to the south afterward does not disqualify them, even if a person carries them there. So the ברייתא's wording 'it jerked and went' cannot mean that carrying it would be a problem. The same wording in the bird ברייתא therefore proves nothing about carrying the bird into the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: a way of showing that the other side's logic leads to a wrong result
Offerings of the most holy level, which are slaughtered in the north of the עזרה
It jerked or convulsed, meaning it moved by itself in its death throes
He took it out, meaning a person moved it on purpose

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning,
regarding offerings of the most sacred order, where it is taught:
if it convulsed, went out to the south, and returned, it is valid;
so if he took it out, would it be disqualified?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 21 by showing that the same reasoning gives a false result in a parallel case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא about a bird that jerked its way into the היכל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא saying 'it went by itself and is valid' does not mean carrying it would disqualify it. The identical wording about the south side clearly does not carry that meaning.

steps.title: The ברייתא was really contrasting with going outside the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: The 'jerked and came back' case is there to contrast with leaving the עזרה, which disqualifies even when it happens by itself. The same is true for the bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this case was needed to contrast with an animal that went outside the עזרה. Here too, the bird case was needed to contrast with one that went outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא even mentions the 'it jerked and moved' case if not to teach about carrying. This completes the rejection of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the ברייתא is a contrast between two places. Moving within the עזרה (to the south, or into the היכל) is fine, but leaving the עזרה disqualifies the offering even if no one carried it. So the wording 'it jerked' is not about 'by itself versus carried', and רבי אבין's question about carrying the bird into the היכל stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: It went outside, meaning beyond the walls of the עזרה
It was needed for him: the teaching was needed for a different purpose
Here too: the same explanation applies to the bird case

steps.whatToRemember: The 'it jerked and came back' ברייתא only teaches that moving inside the עזרה is fine, while leaving it disqualifies. It says nothing about a כהן carrying a bird into the היכל, so רבי אבין's question remains open.

phrases.english: Rather, this was for the case where it went outside;
it was needed for that.
Here too, the case where it went outside;
it was needed for that.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא wants you to learn the opposite case: if it left the עזרה, it is disqualified even though it went by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הַאי יָצְתָה לַחוּץ אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the true purpose of the ברייתא's wording, which finishes the rejection begun in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of the ברייתא's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'it jerked and went' was teaching that a person carrying it in would disqualify it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase is there to contrast with leaving the עזרה, which disqualifies even without a person carrying it. Nothing is proven about carrying it into the היכל.

steps.title: רבי אבין asks about bird blood that spilled and was gathered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין asks: if a bird offering's blood spilled on the floor and the כהן gathered it, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין asked: if the blood spilled on the floor and he gathered it up, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין opens a brand-new question about a bird offering. Its blood spilled on the floor and the כהן scooped it up to sprinkle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bird blood is normally sprinkled straight from the bird's body, not from a כלי שרת. So the question is whether gathering it from the floor is allowed, or whether the blood has to come directly from the bird. The next step lays out the two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked: introduces a real question that the asker is unsure about
It spilled on the floor
He gathered it up

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin asked:
If it spilled on the floor and he gathered it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "It" is the blood of a bird חטאת, still the topic from רבי אבין's earlier question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier question is left unresolved, רבי אבין raises a new question about bird offerings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a bird offering's blood that spilled on the floor and was gathered up is still valid for sprinkling.

steps.title: The two sides: no vessel needed, or a vessel ruled out
steps.stepSummary: Either the תורה just didn't require a כלי שרת, so gathering is fine. Or the תורה ruled out a כלי שרת, so the gathered blood is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did the תורה simply not require a כלי שרת for it, so he may gather it and it is valid? Or perhaps the תורה disqualified a כלי שרת for it, so if he gathers it, it is invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible ways to think about רבי אבין's question. The question is left open here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the תורה only removed the need for a vessel, so blood gathered from the floor is still usable. Side two: the תורה actually ruled out using anything other than the bird itself, so blood gathered from the floor no longer comes straight from the bird and is invalid. The whole question depends on whether 'no vessel' means 'not required' or 'not allowed'.

keyTerms.meaning: A sanctified Temple vessel used for the עבודה
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
To require it
He actually disqualified it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. 'Not required' means a vessel is optional, so the gathered blood is fine. 'Disqualified' means using any vessel is forbidden, so the gathered blood is invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic question in learning: when the תורה exempts something, did it just drop a requirement, or did it forbid the thing?

phrases.aramaic: אַצְרוֹכֵיה הוּא דְּלָא אַצְרְכֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא כְּלִי שָׁרֵת,
phrases.english: Is it that the Merciful One simply did not require a service vessel for it,
and therefore he may gather it and it is valid;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא מִיפְסָל פְּסַל בֵּיהּ רַחֲמָנָא כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת,
phrases.english: or perhaps the Merciful One disqualified a service vessel for it,
and therefore if he gathers it, it is invalid?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַצְרוֹכֵיה הוּא דְּלָא אַצְרְכֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא כְּלִי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two possible reasons behind רבי אבין's question from step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the Torah's not using a כלי שרת for bird blood is only a missing requirement or an actual disqualification of a vessel.

steps.title: רבא's proof from the word 'This'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא that uses 'זאת' to exclude bird-offering blood from כיבוס. He argues this shows a vessel does not disqualify a bird's blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. A ברייתא asks whether the blood of a חטאת העוף needs laundering, and answers no, because the פסוק says 'זאת'. But if the תורה disqualified a vessel for bird blood, we would not need that פסוק. The blood would already be disqualified once it entered the airspace of the garment, which counts as a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer רבי אבין's question (Step 24) by using a ברייתא about washing out bird-offering blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garment counts as a כלי. If any vessel disqualified bird blood, the blood would become invalid the moment it flew into the garment's airspace, and invalid blood needs no כיבוס. Since the ברייתא still needs the word 'זאת' to exempt it, it seems a vessel does not disqualify bird blood, so gathered blood would be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Laundering a garment that had offering blood spray on it
A bird brought as a sin offering
The airspace of a vessel
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהֵא דַּם חַטַּאת הָעוֹף טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס?
phrases.english: One might think the blood of a bird sin offering requires laundering?
So the verse says: "This."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:18. 'This is the law of the sin offering' leaves out the bird.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that the Merciful One disqualified a vessel for it,

phrases.aramaic: תִּיפּוֹק לִי דְּהָא אִפְּסִיל לֵהּ בַּאֲוִיר כְּלִי!
phrases.english: I would know it anyway, since it was already disqualified in the airspace of a vessel!
phrases.notes: The garment counts as a vessel. Once the blood is invalid, it needs no washing, so the פסוק would not be needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the two sides laid out in Step 25 in favor of 'the Torah just did not require a vessel'.
steps.raayaObject: That a vessel does not disqualify bird-offering blood
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that uses 'זאת' to exclude חטאת העוף blood from כיבוס

steps.title: The case of a vessel pressed against the neck
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the פסוק is still needed for a case where the vessel touches the bird's neck directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: the פסוק is talking about a case where the כהן presses a vessel right against the bird's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof by finding a case where 'זאת' is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vessel is pressed onto the neck, the blood goes straight into it without ever passing through a vessel's airspace. So even if a vessel disqualifies bird blood, the 'airspace' reason would not apply here, and the פסוק is needed. רבי אבין's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressing or attaching closely
Neck

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
It is a case where he presses a vessel against its neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע במדביק כלי בצוארה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof. The ברייתא can fit either side of רבי אבין's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed the blood always passes through a vessel's airspace, but there is a case where it does not.

steps.title: Levi asks about blood spraying from one garment to another
steps.stepSummary: לוי asks whether blood that sprays from a first garment onto a second garment still requires כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי asked him: if the blood sprayed from one garment onto another garment, what is the law? Did landing on the first garment push it out of the laundering rule, or perhaps not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of laundering and brings a new question from לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether touching the first garment changes the blood's status. If it does, the second garment would not need washing. If it does not, the second garment needs washing too.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprayed or splashed
Was pushed away, meaning it lost its status
Perhaps

phrases.english: Levi asked him:
phrases.notes: He is asking רבי, רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: If it sprayed from garment to garment, what is the law?
By the first garment, was it pushed out of the laundering rule,
or perhaps not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בעא מיניה לוי ניתז מבגד לבגד מהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about laundering, separate from רבי אבין's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blood that already landed on one garment still requires a second garment to be laundered

steps.title: Either way, the second garment must be laundered
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that the second garment needs כיבוס either way: the blood is either still valid, or it falls under רבי עקיבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is a question! It needs laundering either way. If blood on a garment can be gathered and is valid, then this blood is valid too. And if gathered blood is invalid, I hold like רבי עקיבא, who says: if it had a time when it was valid and then became invalid, its blood still needs laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers לוי's question with a 'whichever way you look at it' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: blood collected from a garment is still valid, so it is plain valid offering blood and needs washing. Option two: it became invalid, but it was valid earlier, when it was collected in the כלי שרת. רבי עקיבא holds that blood which was once valid still requires כיבוס. Both options lead to the same result.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it
He gathers it up
A time when it was valid
It became disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: Blood that sprays from garment to garment still makes the second garment need כיבוס. Either it is still valid, or, like רבי עקיבא says, it was once valid before being disqualified.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is a question!
phrases.notes: It can be read as 'great question!' or as 'what kind of question is that?' Either way, he answers right away.

phrases.english: It requires laundering, whichever way you look at it:
If he can gather it and it is valid, then this is valid.
And if he gathers it and it is invalid,

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְבִירָא לִי, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: I hold like Rabbi Akiva, who says:
if it had a time of being valid and then became invalid,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא but gets left out. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: its blood requires laundering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה זו שאלה טעון כיבוס ממה נפשך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers לוי's question from Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second garment requires כיבוס either way: the blood is either still valid, or it was once valid, and under רבי עקיבא that is enough.
